# tokens: # get / set — universal container access
# `get` and `set` are boru's container-access pair. Both are forward-
# precedence with a fan of signatures so the same word can drive
# Stores (copy-on-write), class instances (in-place mutation),
# FlexMap/FlexList (in-place, returns the node), and plain Map / List / Options nodes
# (read-only for `get`).
# Sig shape (see eng/go/core_storage.go):
#   set 'key' v store      copy-on-write: pushes a new layer with
#                          {'key':v}, propagates up the parent chain.
#   set field v inst       in-place field mutation on a class instance.
#   set i v flexlist       in-place set at index i on a FlexList.
#   set key v map           copy-returning: a NEW map with the key
#                          bound; the receiver Map is untouched (§7).
#   get 'key' store        Store lookup; errors on missing key.
#   get key node           Map/List/Options lookup; missing keys yield
#                          the None type literal.
#   get key inst           class-instance field access.
#   get i flexlist         FlexList element by index.
#   get key None           short-circuits to None — None propagation
#                          for chained reads.
# Map/List read patterns also live in map.tsv / list.tsv. This file
# covers the cross-cutting surface: Store-side set/get via `context`,
# class-instance set, and the None / error paths.
# Runs against the production boru registry.
# 1. Store via `context`: set key value, then read it back
# `set` on a Store is copy-on-write: each set creates a new Store
# layer and propagates the update up through parent layers to the
# context stack. Re-querying the context returns the latest layer.
# Idiom: `context set KEY VAL end` — `context` pushes the current
# context Store onto the stack, `set` then forward-collects KEY and
# VAL, and `end` halts forward collection so the third arg (the
# container) is taken from the stack.
context set 'x' 42 end context get 'x'
note: String key — round-trip through the context store

# tokens: context set ( quote name ) 'Alice' end context get 'name'
note: Atom key — `(quote name)` forces the atom to materialise before set's forward-collection consumes it

# tokens: # Multi-key context — every `set` extends the layer chain, every
# `get` walks it.
context set 'a' 1 end context set 'b' 2 end context get 'a'
note: first key still reachable after second set

# tokens: context set 'a' 1 end context set 'b' 2 end context get 'b'
note: second key visible after its own set

# tokens: # Setting the same key twice — the latest value wins (the new layer
# shadows the old one).
context set 'x' 1 end context set 'x' 2 end context get 'x'
note: shadowing semantics

# tokens: # Store value flows into normal expression flow.
context set 'n' 7 end context get 'n' add 3
note: get-result chains into arithmetic

# tokens: # Missing key on a Store raises an error.
context get 'missing'
note: Store get is strict; missing keys are an error

# 2. Class-instance set
# `set` on a class instance is in-place mutation: the instance's
# field map is updated directly. The instance value held by `def`
# observes the change on subsequent reads.
# String-key set
def Foo (class { a:String b:Integer }) def f (make Foo { a:'hi' b:1 }) set 'a' 'bye' f f .a
note: String key updates the field

# tokens: def Foo (class { a:String b:Integer }) def f (make Foo { a:'hi' b:1 }) set 'a' 'bye' f f .b
note: other fields are untouched

# tokens: # Numeric field via String value — set replaces the value verbatim.
def Foo (class { a:Integer }) def f (make Foo { a:5 }) set 'a' 99 f f .a

# `get key None` yields None — lets chained accessor expressions
# short-circuit through missing levels without crashing.
None get 'a'
note: None passes through string-key access

note: None passes through integer-key access

note: parens isolate each context-get; result is 5+5

# 7. Map set — copy-returning (Map stays immutable)
# `set` on a Map returns a NEW map with the key bound and leaves the
# receiver untouched — the copy-returning contract of push/setpath,
# in contrast to the in-place Store / class-instance forms above (which
# return nothing). Keys are strings or atoms; computed keys via
# parens. Calls chain, so maps build incrementally in a pipeline.
{a:1} set b 2
note: bare-word key binds literally (like class set)

# tokens: {a:1} set 'b' 2
note: string key

# tokens: def k 'dyn' {a:1} set (k) 2
note: computed key — parens take the VALUE of k

# tokens: {a:1} 2 'b' set
note: stack form is equivalent

# tokens: {a:1} set a 9
note: setting an existing key overwrites

# tokens: {} set a 1 set b 2
note: copy-returning means calls chain

# tokens: def m {a:1} def m2 (m set b 2) m
note: the receiver is NOT mutated — m is unchanged

# tokens: def m {a:1} def m2 (m set b 2) m2
note: …the new binding carries the update

note: a bare Map type literal cannot be set

# tokens: # ---- NUR052: enumeration walks the prototype chain, like lookup ----
# A Store's enumeration (`size`, `convert Map`) used to read only the newest
# copy-on-write layer while `get`/`has` walked the full chain, so two sets
# left two keys reachable by lookup and ONE visible to enumeration. One
# store, one keyset, whichever word asks: VisibleKeys walks the chain with
# the SAME precedence Get applies — own layer wins, a tombstone masks
# deeper layers, otherwise the prototype answers.
context set a/q 1 end context set b/q 2 end ((context) has a/q) and ((context) has b/q)
note: both keys answer to lookup, as they always did

# tokens: context set a/q 1 end context set b/q 2 end (size (context)) eq (size (convert Map (context)))
note: …and enumeration now agrees with itself across both words

# tokens: context set a/q 1 end context set b/q 2 end (convert Map (context)) has 'a'
note: the inherited key is ENUMERATED, not just reachable — the divergence this record opened

# tokens: context set k/q 1 end do [context set k/q 2 end (size (context))]
note: MASKING: a child layer shadows the parent's key, so it appears ONCE…

# tokens: context set k/q 1 end do [context set k/q 2 end ((context) get k/q)]
note: …at the CHILD's value, matching what lookup answers

# tokens: context set a/q 1 end context set b/q 2 end context del b/q end ((context) has b/q)
note: a tombstoned key is invisible to lookup…

# tokens: context set a/q 1 end context set b/q 2 end context del b/q end ((convert Map (context)) has 'b')
note: …and to enumeration, by construction — CowDel's layer has no own entry to enumerate

# tokens: context set a/q 1 end context set b/q 2 end context del b/q end ((context) has a/q)
note: the sibling key survives the delete

# tokens: context set a/q 1 end context del a/q end context set a/q 3 end ((context) get a/q)
note: a set AFTER a del revives the key — the own layer is consulted before the tombstone masks deeper ones

# tokens: context set a/q 1 end context del a/q end context set a/q 3 end ((convert Map (context)) has 'a')
note: …and the revival is enumerated too
